cleanIntro: Nothing comes off a 460XVR for cleaning except the compensator, and only on guns fitted with one. What earns the attention on this revolver is the long .460 chamber, because the manual permits two much shorter cartridges in it and both leave a ring behind.

steps.title: Confirm you are holding an X-Frame, not a J, K, L, N or Governor
steps.action: Check that the revolver in front of you is an X-Frame 460 S&W Magnum before using a single step here. This book covers the X-Frame revolvers only; Smith & Wesson prints separate manuals for its J, K, L and N-Frame revolvers, for the Governor, and again for the M&P BODYGUARD 38.
steps.prose: The 460XVR shares the X-Frame with the Model 500 and the Model 350 and is the same book, but nothing here transfers to a .44 Magnum N-frame however alike the two look on a bench. The model name and number are stamped inside the yoke and only visible with the cylinder swung out, so the check costs you the same motion the unload needs anyway.
steps.quote: There are separate manuals for S&W® (J, K, L, N-Frame, and Governor) revolvers and the M&P® BODYGUARD®38 revolver - these manuals are available free upon request or via download from our web site.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Cover page, p.1

steps.title: Thumbpiece forward, cylinder out to the left
steps.action: With your finger off the trigger and outside the trigger guard, press the thumbpiece fully forward and hold it, then push the cylinder out to the left. Check every one of the five charge holes and then sight down the bore from the muzzle.
steps.prose: Hold the thumbpiece forward for the whole swing — releasing it early leaves the cylinder stop dragging in its notch, which people mistake for a jammed gun. On a 460 the charge holes are deep enough that a short .45 Colt case can sit well down one and be easy to miss at a glance, so look into each hole rather than across the cylinder face.
steps.quote: Press the thumbpiece fully forward and hold it, then push the cylinder to the left (FIGURE 5).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Inspecting Your Revolver, p.13

steps.title: Muzzle up, extractor rod through, count what falls
steps.action: Hold the cylinder out with the barrel pointing upward in a safe direction and press the extractor rod firmly through the cylinder, then count what lands in your hand against five charge holes.
steps.prose: Muzzle up is what keeps a partly lifted case from dropping back into its hole where it reads as empty, and on a 460 that is a live possibility because a short 454 Casull or 45 Colt case has a long way to travel before the star has it clear. One full firm stroke lifts all five together; short jabs are what leave one behind.
steps.quote: Carefully count the cartridges or spent casings to be sure that you have recovered all of them.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Unloading, p.27

steps.title: Nothing marked +P+ goes in this revolver
steps.action: Check the headstamps of what you have been firing: ammunition marked +P+ must not be used in this firearm. The 460 S&W Magnum operating at rifle-class pressure does not make a +P+ marking on a 45 Colt box acceptable in it.
steps.prose: The manual's reasoning is that +P+ names no defined pressure limit at all — it is a loader's own marking, so two boxes carrying it can be far apart in what they actually generate. Standard +P is allowed but is warned to affect wear characteristics and bring service forward, which on a revolver shows up first as endshake and a growing barrel/cylinder gap.
steps.caution: "Plus-P-Plus" (+P+) ammunition must NOT be used in Smith & Wesson firearms.
steps.quote: “Plus-P-Plus” (+P+) ammunition must NOT be used in Smith & Wesson® firearms. This marking on the ammunition designates that it exceeds established industry standards, but the designation does not represent defined pressure limits and therefore such ammunition may vary significantly as to the pressures generated and could be DANGEROUS.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Ammunition, +P+ paragraph, p.11

steps.title: Read the barrel marking — 460 S&W MAG, 454 CASULL, 45 COLT and nothing else
steps.action: Read the cartridge designation rolled on your barrel. The manual's alternate-ammunition table lets a revolver marked 460 S&W MAGNUM also fire 454 Casull and 45 Colt, and that three-cartridge list is the whole permission — the manual states in capitals that cartridges other than those specified on the barrel marking may fit into the chambers but must not be used in this firearm, and that injury or death to the shooter or bystanders may result.
steps.prose: That barrel-marking warning is printed under the Model 350 moon-clip heading in this same book, but it is written about the barrel marking on any X-Frame and it is exactly the sentence a 460 owner needs, because this is the one X-Frame whose chamber deliberately accepts more than one cartridge. A .45-calibre case that is not on the three-name list can still drop into the hole and go all the way in.
steps.quote: CARTRIDGES OTHER THAN THOSE SPECIFIED ON THE BARREL MARKING MAY FIT INTO THE CHAMBERS BUT MUST NOT BE USED IN THIS FIREARM. INJURY AND/OR DEATH TO THE SHOOTER OR BYSTANDERS AND DAMAGE TO PROPERTY MAY RESULT.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Ammunition, p.9 (barrel-marking warning at p.20)
steps.warn: Cartridges other than those specified on the barrel marking may fit into the chambers but must not be used in this firearm.

steps.title: If cases dragged on extraction, the chambers are what to clean
steps.action: Think back to how the last cases came out. If extraction was heavy, Smith & Wesson's instruction is to clean the charge holes thoroughly with solvent before you conclude anything about the ammunition, and only change brands if it persists.
steps.prose: This is the 460XVR's characteristic maintenance problem rather than a general note. A cylinder full of 45 Colt or 454 Casull leaves a hard carbon and lead ring partway down a charge hole bored for the much longer .460 case, and the next full-length round has to be forced past it — which feels like tight ammunition and is actually a dirty chamber.
steps.quote: Some brands of ammunition may cause difficulty in extracting spent cartridge cases from the chamber. If this situation occurs, thoroughly clean the chamber with solvent.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Ammunition, p.11

steps.title: Inspect the forcing cone while the cylinder is open
steps.action: With the cylinder swung out, look into the rear of the barrel at the forcing cone and compare what you see against the good and eroded examples the manual prints. This is asked for before use, not just at cleaning time.
steps.prose: The 460 runs the highest velocity of the three X-Frame chamberings and the forcing cone is where that shows first as gas cutting. A smooth even funnel is what you want; flame-cut flats and a ragged crescent at the top mean the barrel goes back to Smith & Wesson for replacement rather than through another cleaning cycle.
steps.quote: Before using a Smith & Wesson® revolver, you should open the cylinder and inspect the barrel forcing cone to ensure that it is in good working condition.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Inspecting Forcing Cone of Smith & Wesson X-Frame Revolvers, p.14

steps.title: If yours wears the removable compensator, take it off
steps.action: Put a 2.5mm hex wrench into the screw under the compensator, below the muzzle opening, and turn it CLOCKWISE until the lock screw stops — about two to three turns. Rotate the compensator a quarter turn either direction with your fingers and draw it forward off the barrel.
steps.prose: This is the only part of a 460XVR the manual takes off the gun, and only on the models fitted with it. The lock screw releases clockwise, the opposite of the reflex that clockwise tightens, so someone turning it the 'undo' way is driving it in harder; if the compensator will not turn by hand, the cross holes in its body take the wrench for leverage.
steps.quote: Remove the compensator from the barrel for cleaning or for a compensator change (FIGURE 34).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Removable Compensator, Removal Instructions, p.29

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have an open, empty cylinder and, if the gun was so fitted, a compensator off the barrel. That is everything Smith & Wesson publishes for the 460XVR — the cylinder, yoke, hammer and lockwork all stay in the frame, and there is no further teardown to reach. Deep Clean carries the record of why for this listing.
steps.prose: The limit is stated in the manual rather than left to inference: it forbids going past the procedure it prints, and it prints no disassembly at all.
steps.quote: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM BEYOND THE FIELD STRIPPING/DISASSEMBLY PROCEDURE DETAILED IN THIS MANUAL, OR PERFORM ANY MAINTENANCE, ADJUSTMENT, OR SERVICE NOT SPECIFIED.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Cleaning and Maintenance, p.31

deepAbsentReason: The X-Frame manual documents opening and unloading the cylinder, inspecting the forcing cone, removing and refitting the removable compensator, cleaning, lubrication and storage — and publishes no disassembly of the revolver whatsoever. Its table of contents carries no field-stripping or disassembly section at all, and p.31 forbids going beyond what it prints.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHARGE HOLES
tasks: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and all five charge holes with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Where 454 Casull or 45 Colt has been fired, brush the full depth of each charge hole to break the carbon ring the shorter case leaves partway down
Finish each with a dry cotton patch to carry out residue and solvent
Clean the cylinder face and the underside of the extractor star

cleaning.name: COMPENSATOR (IF FITTED)
tasks: With the compensator off, clean its bore channel and ports of carbon and lead
Clean the muzzle end of the barrel it seats on, along with the lock screw and notch
Use the compensator pattern that matches what you shoot — one is specified for jacketed bullets, the other for lead

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Clean the exterior with a non-abrasive cloth
Remove all gun cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints from outside surfaces — finger moisture left on steel starts a corrosion process
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning
Never use ammoniated or other strong alkaline solvents on this revolver

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION AND STORAGE
tasks: After cleaning, lightly coat the metal parts, internal and external, with a high quality gun oil
In a cold climate choose an oil weight that will not congeal and slow the action
For extended storage oil the bore, charge holes and internal mechanism, and coat the external mechanism and barrel with an anti-rust oil
Do not store the revolver in leather or heavy cloth, and never with a plug in the barrel
Check for signs of wear every time you clean it; if wear is noted, do not use the revolver

reassembly: If the compensator was removed: insert it into the front of the barrel shroud, rotate it with your fingers until the notch faces down in the 6 o'clock position, then hold it and turn the 2.5mm hex wrench COUNTERCLOCKWISE until the lock screw stops — two to three turns. Do not overtighten.
Close the cylinder into the frame and confirm it locks up.
Clean the revolver again before firing if it has been in long storage.
fncheck: With all five charge holes confirmed empty and the bore clear, close the cylinder and check that it latches and that the thumbpiece releases it cleanly. Cycle the action double action and single action pointed in a safe direction, confirming the cylinder indexes and locks at every stop and that hammer and trigger return to the at-rest forward position. Inspect the forcing cone and the barrel/cylinder gap every time you clean; if wear is noted, do not use the revolver.
